analysis:
The supplied changes are confined to the test file provider-swift/Tests/ProviderCoreTests/Inference/Engine/EngineV2ProductionWiringTests.swift. Per the patch, the diff has four parts. (1) The test event switch at line 312 now also ignores `.toolCallDelta`. (2) `makeThinkProbeEngine` takes an optional `modelType` parameter (lines 1308 and 1322). (3) Two new parameterized tests for qwen3_5 and qwen3_5_moe (lines 1365-1376) assert that a plain tail keeps close-only output undecided. (4) A Qwen3-VL test (lines 1378-1390) asserts that a plain assistant tail seeds `<think></think>` content state. I reviewed the displayed units, which cover lines 655-1817 of the head file. They include the KV re-slice and grant tests, paged vs contiguous pool accounting, the re-slice gate regression test, heartbeat tracking, and the request-routing and tool-choice tests.

No production code is changed, and no trust boundary, key handling, attestation, authorization, encryption, or cache-scope logic is altered. Test fixtures use stub tokenizers and scripted engines only. The TB-007/T-041 cacheSalt plumbing test (line 1754) is unchanged in meaning, and the fail-closed tool-choice tests still assert that no engine submission or exposure occurs on violation.

Open integration questions: the production-side change that the `.toolCallDelta` event and the Qwen3-VL seeding behavior imply is in other files, not supplied here. The next pass should check whether that code emits tool-call deltas before forced `tool_choice` validation, because that could leak unvalidated visible output. That is outside this test-only diff and cannot be assessed from this evidence. The patch excerpt is truncated, so the full test additions were not seen in patch form.
